Subject: Renewal timing and capacity needs for 2027

Aditya —

Thanks for the quick catch-up last week. Our executive team asked me to get a formal proposal that addresses three constraints before we can move to procurement: (1) a multi-year option that doesn’t lock us into an over-commit in year 1, (2) an ability to phase in additional capacity tied to clear usage triggers, and (3) a simple auto-renew opt-out process on year-to-year pricing.

Current thinking on our side: we want a 36-month umbrella agreement, but we prefer a graduated ramp (smaller Year 1 commitment, larger Year 3). We also need a clear mid-term option to convert reserved commit into burstable capacity for pilot workloads.

Can you outline a structure (pricing + practical ops steps) we can present to procurement? attaching a short note from our CFO.

Thanks,
Kathryn
Head of NLP Platforms
Veridian Health

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timing and capacity needs for 2027

Kathryn —

Appreciate the clarity. I pulled together a proposal that tries to hit all three asks while minimizing year-one overhang. High level:

- Agreement footprint: 36-month Master Services Agreement + three annual purchase schedules.
- Variable-tenor commitment: define an effective committed consumption floor per year (Year1: 40% of target, Year2: 75%, Year3: 100%) with blended unit pricing that rewards sustained commit.
- Phased top-up: three phase gates (Q1, Q3, Year2) that allow Veridian to convert pre-allocated credits into dedicated capacity at pre-agreed better-than-overage rates.
- Mid-term switch: optional conversion clause to move up to 30% of remaining reserved capacity into burstable pool with a 30-day notice and proration.
- Auto-renew: default auto-renew with an explicit 60-day opt-out window and a capped annual CPI+ structural adjustment (no surprises).

Operational notes:
- We’ll supply an implementation checklist (onboarding slots, traffic routing, KV cache warm-up plan) and a capacity orchestration runbook for any mid-term conversions.
- SLA credits for latency/availability regressions are tiered; if you hit trigger X (monthly 99.5% token SLO miss), a partial credit applies and we prioritize capacity scaling.

I attached the worksheet with a few pricing scenarios and a worked example for a 3x ramp. If this looks good, I can convert the winning scenario into a redline-ready amendment and loop in Legal & Procurement.

Next steps I propose: quick internal alignment call tomorrow (short) so we can produce a single doc for your procurement team by Friday.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Lead — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Variable-Tenor-Proposal-v1.xlsx (xlsx), Veridian_MAAP_v2.pdf (pdf)
